extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and USPTO examiners handling accelerated/prioritized examination requests
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for filing and prosecuting U.S. patent applications under the USPTO accelerated (petition to make special) and prioritized examination programs, including eligibility, required documents, timing goals, procedural limits, and required form/filing practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: After-Final and Appeal Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: The mailing of a final Office action or the filing of a notice of appeal, whichever is earlier, is the final disposition for purposes of the twelve-month goal for the accelerated examination program. Prior to the mailing of a final Office action, the USPTO will conduct a conference to review the rejections set forth in the final Office action. In order for the application to be expeditiously forwarded to the Board of Patent Appeals and Interferences (BPAI) for a decision, applicant must: (A) promptly file the notice of appeal, appeal brief, and appeal fees; and (B) not request a pre-appeal brief conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A pre-appeal brief conference would not be of value in an application under a final Office action because the examiner will have already conducted such a conference prior to mailing the final Office action. During the appeal process, the application will be treated in accordance with normal appeal procedures (MPEP Chapter 1200). The USPTO will continue to treat the application as special under the accelerated examination program after the decision by the BPAI.

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE treated as final disposition for twelve-month goal
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant files a request for continued examination (RCE) under 37 CFR 1.114 with a submission and fee, the filing of the RCE is a final disposition for purposes of the twelve-month goal for the accelerated examination program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The RCE submission must meet the reply requirements under 37 CFR 1.111 and the requirements set forth in subsection IV. The application will retain its special status and remain in the accelerated examination program; the examiner will continue to examine the application according to accelerated procedures. The goal is to reach final disposition within twelve months from the filing of the RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings outside normal examination (pause in acceleration)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application becomes involved in proceedings outside the normal examination process (e.g., a secrecy order, national security review, interference, or petitions under 37 CFR 1.181, 1.182, or 1.183), the USPTO will treat the application special but the application will not be accelerated during those proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During such proceedings the application is treated according to the applicable normal procedures (e.g., interference procedures). Once the external proceeding is completed, the USPTO will process the application expeditiously under the accelerated examination program until final disposition, although that may occur later than twelve months from filing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any non-reissue utility or design application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after August 25, 2006 is eligible for the accelerated examination program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The following are not eligible: (1) plant applications; (2) reissue applications; (3) applications entering the national stage from an international application after compliance with 35 U.S.C. 371; (4) reexamination proceedings; (5) RCEs under 37 CFR 1.114 (unless the application was previously granted special status under the program); and (6) petitions to make special based on applicant’s health or age or under the PPH pilot program. Design applicants may instead use the expedited examination program under MPEP § 1504.30 and 37 CFR 1.155.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form to file petition to make special (PTO/SB/28)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant should use form PTO/SB/28 for filing a petition to make special (other than those based on applicant’s health or age or the PPH pilot program).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The form is available on EFS-Web and on the USPTO’s Internet Web site at http://www.uspto.gov/web/forms/index.html.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application must be in condition for examination at filing (conditions for examination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must be in condition for examination at the time of filing. This means the application must include specified items (see list).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required items include: (1) basic filing fee, search fee, and examination fee (37 CFR 1.16); (2) application size fee if >100 sheets (37 CFR 1.16(s)); (3) an executed oath or declaration (37 CFR 1.63); (4) a specification (37 CFR 1.52) containing a description (37 CFR 1.71) and claims (37 CFR 1.75); (5) a title and an abstract (37 CFR 1.72); (6) drawings (37 CFR 1.84); (7) electronic submissions of sequence listings, large tables, or computer listings via EFS in ASCII text if applicable (37 CFR 1.821(c)/(e), 1.96); (8) foreign priority claim under 35 U.S.C. 119(a)-(d) identified in the executed oath/declaration or application data sheet if applicable; (9) domestic benefit claims under 35 U.S.C. 119(e),120,121, or 365(c) in compliance with 37 CFR 1.78 (specific reference placement rules and translation statement for benefit to non-English provisional applications) if applicable; (10) English translation and accuracy statement plus processing fee if specification in non-English (37 CFR 1.52(d), 1.17(i)); (11) no preliminary amendments present on the filing date; and (12) no petition under 37 CFR 1.47 for a non-signing inventor. For design applications, comply with 37 CFR 1.151-1.154. Applicant should also provide a suggested classification by class/subclass on the transmittal letter, petition, or application data sheet (37 CFR 1.76(b)(3)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition dismissal for formality omissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The petition to make special will be dismissed if the application omits an item or includes a paper that causes the Office of Patent Application Processing (OPAP) to mail a notice during the formality review (e.g., notice of incomplete application, to file missing parts, to file corrected papers, notice of omitted items, or notice of informal application).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The opportunity to perfect a petition (subsection II) does not apply to applications that are not in condition for examination on filing. The twelve-month goal related matters are neither petitionable nor appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reply not fully responsive — shortened time and abandonment risk
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reply to a non-final Office action is not fully responsive, but is a bona fide attempt to advance the application to final action, the examiner may provide one month or thirty days, whichever is longer, for applicant to supply the omission or a fully responsive reply. No extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) will be permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to timely file the omission or a fully responsive reply will result in abandonment of the application. If the reply is not a bona fide attempt or it is a reply to a final Office action, no additional time period will be given. The time period set forth in the previous Office action will continue to run.

rubrics_metrics.name: No withdrawal from accelerated examination
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no provision for 'withdrawal' from special status under the accelerated examination program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An applicant may abandon the special-status application in favor of a continuing application; the continuing application will not be given special status unless the continuing application is filed with a petition to make special. Filing an RCE under 37 CFR 1.114 will not result in withdrawal from special status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Twelve-month goal: dispositions that satisfy goal
rubrics_metrics.description: The objective of the accelerated examination program is to complete examination within twelve months from the filing date. The twelve-month goal is successfully achieved when one of the following final dispositions occurs: (1) mailing of a notice of allowance; (2) mailing of a final Office action; (3) filing of an RCE; or (4) abandonment of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final disposition may occur later than twelve months in certain situations (e.g., an IDS citing new prior art after mailing of first Office action). The twelve-month time frame is a goal; failure to meet it or other issues relating to it are not petitionable/appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirement for replies (EFS-Web) to preserve expedited processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reply must be filed electronically via EFS-Web so that the papers will be expeditiously processed and considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the reply is not filed electronically via EFS-Web, the final disposition of the application may occur later than twelve months from filing. Form paragraphs repeatedly instruct electronic filing and note that electronic filing is required for certain eligibility paths (e.g., prioritized examination utility applications).

rubrics_metrics.name: Updated preexamination search and accelerated examination support documents required for claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: For any amendments to the claims (including any new claim) that is not encompassed by the preexamination search and accelerated examination support documents previously filed, applicant is required to provide updated preexamination search and accelerated examination support documents that encompass the amended or new claims at the time of filing the amendment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide such updated support documents at time of filing the amendment will cause the amendment to be treated as not fully responsive and not to be entered (see MPEP § 708.02(a) subsection VIII.D.). Form paragraphs 7.70.AE and 7.71.AE must be included in every Office action (other than notice of allowance) for applicable special-status applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper document and fee codes when filing via EFS-Web
rubrics_metrics.description: Any reply or other papers filed via EFS-Web must include a document filed using the Transmittal description of 'Accelerated Exam amendment/reply' and must use proper indexing for documents to avoid processing delays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document indexing in EFS-Web is not automated; applicants must select the correct description for each attached file. Incorrect document description or improper fee code selection may delay processing. A complete listing of document codes and fee/payment instructions are provided by USPTO (links cited in MPEP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listings and CRF (computer readable form) compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications containing nucleotide and/or amino acid sequence disclosures must comply with 37 CFR 1.821 through 1.825 (sequence rules) and, if applicable, submit electronic sequence listings/CRF submissions in the required format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sequence disclosures are present and the application fails to comply with 1.821-1.825, applicant is given ONE (1) MONTH or THIRTY (30) DAYS (whichever is longer) to comply; failure results in abandonment under 37 CFR 1.821(g). If a CRF could not be processed (CRF Diskette Problem Report), applicant must correct and return the report. Use the specified form paragraphs for initial vs subsequent communications, attach marked-up copies of raw sequence listings, and follow MPEP §§ 710.02(c), 711.02(a), 714.02 and 714.03 and 37 CFR 1.135(c), 1.821(g).

rubrics_metrics.name: RCE eligibility and timing requirements under 37 CFR 1.114 for accelerated program use
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for continued examination under 37 CFR 1.114, the application must be a utility or plant application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) on or after June 8, 1995, or an international application filed under 35 U.S.C. 363 on or after June 8, 1995. The RCE must be filed on or after May 29, 2000.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraph 7.42.08.AE to acknowledge an RCE filed with a submission that is not fully responsive (bona fide attempt). In bracketed text the examiner should identify why the submission is not fully responsive. This form paragraph may be used for any RCE filed with a submission which is not fully responsive, e.g., after final rejection, after allowance, after Ex parte Quayle, or after appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritized Examination (37 CFR 1.102(e)) requirements and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: A request for prioritized examination under 37 CFR 1.102(e) must comply with the paragraph and be accompanied by the prioritized examination fee under § 1.17(c), the processing fee under § 1.17(i), and, if not already paid, the publication fee under § 1.18(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application for prioritized examination may not contain or be amended to contain more than four independent claims, more than thirty total claims, or any multiple dependent claim. Prioritized examination will not be accorded to international applications that have not entered the national stage under 35 U.S.C. 371, design applications, reissue applications, provisional applications, or reexamination proceedings. A request for prioritized examination may be filed with an original utility or plant nonprovisional application that is complete as defined by § 1.51(b), with any fees due under § 1.16 paid on filing. If the application is a utility application, it must be filed via the Office's electronic filing system. The request for prioritized examination must be present upon filing of the application and must also comply with paragraph (e)(1) or (e)(2).
